text: {"summary":"Task: choose one listed color for each of v1–v9 in order, with different colors on every supplied edge, and return a nine-entry values array. Bounds are integers 0–2. Allowed-color lists are v1 [1,0], v2 [0,1], v3 [0,1], v4 [1,0], v5 [2,0], v6 [2,0], v7 [0,2], v8 [2,0], v9 [1,2]. Edges (zero-based indices) are [0,2], [0,5], [0,7], [1,4], [1,7], [2,4], [2,5], [2,7], [2,8], [3,4], [3,5], [3,6], [3,7], [5,8], [6,8]. A constraint-search trial selected the listed colors in order and reported that every edge had differently colored endpoints. It encoded [0,1], [0,2], [1,0], [1,2], [2,0] as integers 1–5, yielding values [3,1,1,3,5,5,2,5,4]. Public feedback rejected this candidate: status public_mismatch, check bound1, observed 3, expected [0,2], detail “Candidate is outside the declared integer bounds.” The encoding was an assumption, not specified by the task, and the candidate violates the declared bounds. The requirement remains to find a representation of listed colors compatible with the integer bounds and return valid values; the record does not establish that the graph coloring itself is impossible."}
